scope: Proposition 3.3 (Divisorial normalization) of the manuscript “Logarithmic Kodaira dimension and whole-fiber variation” (preprints/Logarithmic-Kodaira-dimension-and-whole-fiber-variation-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 033 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9b1b750b309e5c5a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For a prime divisor P on W, and for a prime divisor Q on the actual source X′ dominating P, set (3.5) mQ = ordQ(x∗ P), rQ = 1 p ordQ(ωJ ), dQ = coeffQ(D′ ), tP = min Q7→P Q on X′ rQ + dQ mQ , λP = inf Q7→P 1 + rQ mQ , BP = 1 − λP + tP . In the definition of λP , Q runs over divisorial valuations on all higher smooth source models. In both formulas rQ is measured in the actual relative canonical bundle with respect to the smooth base W. The two rational divisors T = X P tP P, B = X P BP P have finite support. The divisor B is an effective boundary and (3.6) 0 ≤ BP ≤ 1, B ≥ D0 W = (g∗ DY )red. The formulas at unchanged codimension-one base points are invariant under further source res- olutions with the prescribed boundary convention. They are also preserved, allowing splitting of components, by an étale extension of the base DVR and the corresponding source base change. After a further birational preparation of W, B can be assumed to have SNC support.
